records.summary: Mapped a repeated five-hop XRPL transfer corridor from a Ripple-labelled wallet family through three unlabelled intermediaries to a Bithomp-labelled Bitso account using a consistent destination tag. The route is consistent with an institutional payment/liquidity corridor and is strategically relevant because Ripple publicly documents a long-standing Bitso ODL partnership and a 2026 expansion involving XRP, RLUSD and MXNB. The transaction route is not proven to be Ripple Payments/ODL; no fiat leg or customer instruction was identified. Also corrected the '310M Ripple outflow' headline: it adds two inbound transfers to one outbound transfer and is gross, not net, flow.
actions: Inspected Bithomp transaction pages for rJqi, rP4X2h, rhWt2bh and r4wf7en.
Resolved one Ripple-rooted activation chain for the 90M XRP source and one unlabelled activation chain for the 99.999999M XRP source.
Verified repeated tagged deposits from r4wf7en into the Bithomp-labelled Bitso account.
Cross-referenced the observed route against Ripple's 2019 ODL/Bitso announcement, 2019 investment announcement and June 2026 partnership expansion.
Separated gross transfer volume from net account flow and preserved non-ODL alternative hypotheses.
blockers: No Ripple Payments/ODL message ID or fiat settlement leg links the observed route to a named customer payment.
The intermediary accounts are unlabelled and beneficial owners are unknown.
Bitso destination tag 88409288 is not attributed to a customer or institution.
No same-unit provenance across intermediaries or proof of completed MXN payout.
next_actions: Monitor the repeated route and compare future timing/amounts without assuming one-to-one pass-through.
Search public Ripple/Bitso disclosures and filings for current corridor volumes, counterparties and product-specific rails.
Determine whether the Bitso destination tag is a public institutional/operational tag; do not attempt private identity resolution.
Compare this Bitso route with the separate raRVLN→r39TA→Binance route and test whether they share any public wallet-control evidence.
